name: MonarchColumnsBlock
title: ColumnsBlock
summary: Two or more side-by-side columns inside a document, which stack into one column where the width is narrow.
whenToUse: To set two short passages next to each other in a document or an article, such as a before and an after, or three steps of a plan.
whenNotToUse: For a split the user resizes use MonarchResizablePanels. For a screen layout that adapts to the window use the Material 3 adaptive panes. For tabular data use MonarchTableBlock.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchColumnsBlock(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, ratio: Float = MonarchColumnsBlockTokens.DEFAULT_RATIO, content: MonarchColumnsBlockScope.() -> Unit)
public sealed interface MonarchColumnsBlockScope { public fun column(content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit) }

options.name: ratio
options.description: The share of the width for the first of two columns, kept between 0.2 and 0.8 (0.5 when not a number). Three or more columns are equal.

options.name: content
options.description: Declares the columns with column { }, in order. Each column lays its content out top to bottom.

states.name: side by side
states.description: From 480dp of available width at the default font size, the columns sit next to each other with a 24dp gap, top-aligned.

states.name: stacked
states.description: Below that width, or with one column, the columns stack in order with a 12dp gap. The 480dp threshold is multiplied by the font scale, so at font scale 2.0 a block narrower than 960dp stacks.

appearance: No surface of its own: the columns sit on whatever is behind the block, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web ColumnsBlock is also a Tiptap editor node with a resize handle that writes the ratio into the document; Android has no Monarch rich-text editor, so only the static block is offered, as on iOS. For a split the user resizes, MonarchResizablePanels exists. The web stacks with a container query at 30rem; Android uses the width offered to the block, 30 times the base type size (480dp), scaled by the font scale as rem is scaled by the browser text size. iOS takes each child view as a column; on Android columns are declared with column { } in a builder scope, as items are in a LazyColumn, so each column can be made a TalkBack traversal group. The parity plan lists resizable-panels as a dependency; it is not used, because the block has no handle.
accessibility: Each column is a TalkBack traversal group, so TalkBack reads one column completely before the next instead of reading across the columns line by line.
Columns are placed from the start edge, so the first column is on the right in right-to-left layouts.
At large font sizes the columns stack sooner, so text keeps a readable width; text is never cut.
edgeCases: One column fills the width; an empty block takes no height.
A column taller than the others sets the height of the block; the others stay at the top.
Inside a horizontally scrolling container, which offers no width limit, the block assumes 480dp.
Content added outside column { } is not shown: the builder only collects columns.
